title: IAM privilege provisioning strategy and hosting-tier rules
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic provisioning strategy for IAM roles and privileges across Redwood's three hosting tiers (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It focuses on: minimizing blast radius, enabling automated evidence collection for audits, and producing a SIEM-friendly audit export schema.

Context / Why different than previous matrix files:
- Existing artifacts enumerate roles and policies; this doc is an operational roadmap that ties role assignment to provisioning flows, automated evidence (attachments/logs), and SIEM mappings.
- Emphasis on lifecycle (request -> approval -> provisioning -> evidence snapshot -> periodic re-approval).

High-level principles:
- Least privilege by default, staged escalation via ephemeral grants (just-in-time) for sensitive ops.
- Role families (Admin, Platform Operator, Support Analyst, Dev, ReadOnly, Billing) reused across tiers but scoped differently.
- Evidence-first: every grant must produce an evidence bundle (policy diff, approval ticket, requester identity, time window) pushed to audit storage.
- Deterministic SIEM fields for downstream detection and reporting.

Role families and recommended scoping by hosting tier (compact table):
- Admin: full control over customer resources.
  - Hosted: limited to organization-level config, no tenant key access; require 2-person approval.
  - Dedicated: org-level + project-level ops; tenant key access only with explicit SLA ticket.
  - Private: generally gated; privileged admin only on customer request with contract clause.
- Platform Operator: deployment, scaling, runtime tuning.
  - Hosted: allowed on infra projects, cannot access tenant data keys.
  - Dedicated: allowed per-dedicated-pool if assigned; needs schedule-based just-in-time grant for hotfixes.
  - Private: on-prem operator access provided through customer's onboarding handshake; use temporary certificates.
- Support Analyst: user/route debugging, logs, non-sensitive telemetry.
  - Hosted: read-only to tenant metadata and debug traces (PII redacted).
  - Dedicated: per-customer support tunnels with audit triggers.
  - Private: support access only via recorded session and with customer consent.
- Dev: code-level repo and infra testing access.
  - Hosted: sandbox projects and can request ephemeral staging creds.
  - Dedicated/Private: no direct tenant access by default.
- ReadOnly: universal read-only across non-secret resources.
- Billing: access to usage and billing dashboards; cannot modify resources.

Policy template examples (cut-down snippets; replace placeholders before use):
- Least-privilege policy granting List/Describe for compute pools (example JSON snippet):
  {
    "Version": "2023-01-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["compute:ListPools", "compute:DescribePool"],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:compute:${region}:${account}:pool/${pool_id}"
      }
    ]
  }

- Time-bound elevated grant (example pseudo-API request payload):
  {
    "principal": "user:alice@example.com",
    "role": "platform-operator",
    "scope": "project:infra-east",
    "granted_for": "2h",
    "approval_ticket": "JIRA-OPS-456"
  }

Provisioning lifecycle (recommended flow):
1) Request created via self-service portal or ticket (Jira/ServiceNow). Request metadata includes: requester, justification, affected resources, requested duration, linked PR/CI job if relevant.
2) Automated pre-checks: policy collision, existing overlapping grants, asset sensitivity check.
3) Approval gates: role-dependent. Low-risk (ReadOnly) auto-approve; mid/high-risk require 1 or 2 approvers respectively.
4) Provisioner issues ephemeral creds or attaches role. Provisioner stores a snapshot: policy-attached, principal, before/after IAM diff, approver IDs, ticket link, TTL. Snapshot is pushed to evidence store (immutable object storage) with a unique evidence_id.
5) SIEM export (see schema below) emits a SIEM event with evidence_id, and K/V fields used by detection rules.
6) Reconciliation job verifies active grants against snapshots daily; mismatches trigger remediation ticket and attach the last-known evidence snapshot.

Audit log / SIEM export schema (canonical event fields — guaranteed present):
- event_time: RFC3339 timestamp
- event_type: grant_request | grant_approve | grant_revoke | grant_expire | policy_change
- principal_id: canonical user/service id
- principal_type: user | service | machine
- role_name: e.g., platform-operator
- resource_scope: canonical ARN or project id
- granting_actor: who performed action (system, approver id)
- approval_ticket: ticket id or URL (nullable)
- evidence_id: object id in evidence bucket (required for audit records)
- ttl_seconds: seconds until automatic expiry (nullable)
- before_policy_hash: sha256 of previous policy blob (nullable)
- after_policy_hash: sha256 of new policy blob (nullable)
- request_id: correlation id
- hosting_tier: hosted | dedicated | private
- control_flags: comma-separated flags (e.g., just_in_time, manual_approval, customer_consent)

SIEM export format recommendations:
- Primary export is newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Keep fields stable (no ad-hoc keys).
- Push a minimal flattened record to SIEM and attach evidence_id to allow analysts to fetch raw snapshots from secure object store.
- Example ndjson line: {"event_time":"2025-02-12T18:03:12Z","event_type":"grant_approve","principal_id":"user:diego@redwood.ai","role_name":"platform-operator","resource_scope":"project:dedicated-pool-eu-1","evidence_id":"evid_20250212_8a3f","hosting_tier":"dedicated"} 

Evidence bundle contents (what the provisioner must capture):
- policy_blobs: previous and new (raw JSON)
- ticket: snapshot (HTML or plaintext) of approval/justification
- requester identity and SSO assertion (OIDC token claim subset)
- temporal metadata (requested_for, created_at, expires_at)
- environment snapshot (deployment hashes, region, pool id)
- operator session recording link (if interactive) or CI job link
- digest file (sha256 list of all files)

Automated evidence ingestion flow (sketch):
- provisioner finishes grant -> creates evidence bundle -> signs metadata with service key -> uploads bundle to evidence-bucket/evid_{id}.tar.gz -> emits SIEM event with evidence_id -> ticket updated automatically with link.
- Small script example (pseudo-Bash):
  EVID_ID=$(uuidgen)
  tar -czf /tmp/$EVID_ID.tar.gz policy_before.json policy_after.json ticket.html assertion.json meta.json
  aws s3 cp /tmp/$EVID_ID.tar.gz s3://redwood-evidence/evid_$EVID_ID.tar.gz --acl bucket-owner-full-control
  curl -XPOST https://siem-push.redwood.ai/events -d "{\"event_time\":\"$(date -u +%FT%TZ)\",\"event_type\":\"grant_approve\",\"evidence_id\":\"$EVID_ID\",...}"

Re-approval and periodic review cadence suggestions:
- High-privilege grants: 30-day forced re-approval and must include recent justification and evidence snapshot.
- Mid-privilege grants: 90-day re-approval.
- Low-privilege/read-only: 180-day review.

Detection and alerting ideas (SIEM rules tied to schema):
- Unexpected long-lived ephemeral grants: TTL > 24h for a just_in_time flag -> alert.
- Grant without evidence_id -> immediate failed-audit ticket.
- Policy delta that increases principal set or expands resource globs -> high-priority review.
- Cross-tier admin grant where hosting_tier mismatch occurs (e.g., a host-admin grant on private without customer_consent) -> block and alert.

Customer-facing contract considerations (Private deployments):
- Access-lock: require explicit customer-signed opt-in for Redwood support staff to be granted private cluster admin privileges. Evidence snapshots must be delivered to customer S3/ftp.
- Onboarding handshake: include clear TTLs and emergency escalation process.

Open questions / TODOs (working items):
- Decide canonical evidence storage encryption envelope (KMS per-tier vs org KMS).
- Standardize approver tiers and map to people manager org structure.
- Build small POC provisioner Lambda that creates evidence bundles and sends ndjson messages to SIEM.

Appendix: quick checklist for ship-ready policy rollout
- [ ] Define role family mapping for 3rd-party integrations (monitoring, backups).
- [ ] Implement evidence snapshot writer in provisioner (json + signed manifest).
- [ ] Add SIEM ndjson schema validation on ingestion pipeline.
- [ ] Create guardrails in self-service portal to prevent granting admin role on private clusters without documented customer consent.

If you are reviewing: please annotate sections you plan to own, call out policy snippet tweaks specific to your cloud provider, and link any existing ticket that should be the canonical implementation issue.

End of working doc.
